newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices up, budget hopes flare.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices up, budget hopes flare.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds gained 1/8 to 1/4 point in spots, turning around with U.S. Treasury bonds on hopes that the Republican Congress and President Bill Clinton were closer to a budget.
U.S. Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott said that negotiators were "very close" on a budget deal but it would not be perfect.

Still, this type of guarded optimism helped fixed-income markets rebound from early losses incurred after the latest data on the nation's economy showed unexepected strength. The first quarter Real Gross Domestic Product was pegged at up 5.6 percent, with the implicit price deflator rising 2.3 percent.
The rise in the GDP, the biggest in nine years, exceeded forecasts for a 4.1 percent increase, according to a Reuters consensus poll.

Traders noted that activity was fairly subdued, with some municipal bonds not fully capturing the gains. "We're lethargic," a trader said. "I'd say we're up at least an eighth of a point to a quarter in spots," he added.

Traders said there were few if any bid wanted lists being circulated, although they noted that the market appeared to have a fairly strong appetite for new offerings, including Tuesday's $701 million sale by the New York City Municipal Water Finance Authority.
"We're able to digest everything that's coming well," another trader said.
Municipal bond sales for Wednesday were expected to total $445 million in 18 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.

Negotiated offerings total $389 million in 10 sales, with a $155 million Lorain County, Ohio deal through Bear, Stearns & Co. Inc., topping the list. The debt was priced at a top yield of 5.875 percent in 2027.

On the competitive side, eight sales totaling $60 million were on the schedule. A $17 million Kent County, Mich., deal at 1100 EDT was the largest, and was won at a net interest cost of 6.55 percent, according to winning bidder Smith Barney Inc.
In the secondary market, Chicago Board of Education School Reform bonds of December 2020, which pay a 5-3/4 percent coupon, were bid at 5.97 percent, NET, up one basis point.

And Minnesota Agricultural and Economic Development Board Revenue Health Care System, Fairview Hospital of November 2026, which have a 5-3/4 percent coupon, were bid at 5.91 percent, NET, down six basis points.
In debt futures, June municipal futures rose 17 ticks to 114-15/32, while June Treasury bonds climbed 20 ticks to 109-18/32. This left the MOB spread was at plus 156 ticks.
